One program, two (or more) machines

The placement pass builds symbol, effect, data, and security graphs, then assigns each function to browser / server / edge / worker / shared. Secrets, DB drivers, and privileged imports pin their module to the server — the compiler errors instead of leaking.

from pyweb import App, server


app = App()


@server
def get_count() -> int:
    return 42


@app.page("/")
def Home():
    new_todo = ""
    todos = ["buy milk", "ship pyweb"]


    def add():
        todos = todos


    <main>
        <h1>Todos</h1>
        <input bind={new_todo} />
        <button onclick={add}>
            Add
        </button>
        for todo in todos:
            <label>
                {todo}
            </label>
    </main>

import { sig, computed, bind_text, bind_input, on, rpc, mutate, liveList, liveIf, takeover, dynText } from './runtime.js';

export const new_todo = sig(""); // pyweb:new_todo
export const todo = sig(null); // pyweb:todo
export const todos = sig(["buy milk", "ship pyweb"]); // pyweb:todos
export function add(e) { todos(todos()) } // pyweb-line:18
async function get_count() {
  return rpc('get_count', {});
} // rpc:get_count pyweb-line:8
window.__pyweb_scope = { add, new_todo, todo, todos };
export function mount(root=document) {
  // static — no bindings
  bind_input(root, "new_todo", 'pw00001'); // line 24
  on(root, 'click', add, 'pw00002'); // line 25
  // static — no bindings
  // live-for hid 22 (line 28): SSR rows activate below
  (() => { const __anchor = takeover(root, 22);
    const __row = (todo, __i, __key) => {
      const __frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
  bind_text(__frag, "todo", () => (todo())); // line 30
      return { els: Array.from(__frag.childNodes) }; };
    liveList(__anchor, () => (todos()), (__item, __i, __key) => __row(__item, __i, __key), ((todo) => (todo()))); })();
}
if (typeof document !== 'undefined') {
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => mount(document));
  } else { mount(document); }
}

<main><h1>Todos</h1><input data-pw-id="pw00001"><button data-pw-id="pw00002">Add</button><label><span pw-bind="todo">buy milk</span></label><label><span pw-bind="todo">ship pyweb</span></label></main>

Generated RPC contract

Python annotations are the contract — no OpenAPI files, no DTO duplication. What the compiler derived from the todo app above:

FunctionArgsReturnsRuns onDefined
get_count—intserverline 8

Placement decisions with reasons

Same output as pyweb inspect — every symbol, its location, and why:

add → browser event handler reachable from UI, browser-safe deps
new_todo → browser reactive UI state read by markup, mutated by events
todo → browser reactive UI state read by markup, mutated by events
todos → browser reactive UI state read by markup, mutated by events
__page__ → browser+server SSR initial HTML on server, activation in browser

Failure semantics stay visible: the stub propagates auth headers, sends CSRF tokens, retries only idempotent calls, honors timeouts and cancellation, and maps server error codes back to Python exceptions with source-mapped tracebacks. RPC feels local; it never lies about being remote.
Safety rule: when the compiler is unsure where code can safely run, it keeps it on the server. Overrides (@browser @server @edge @worker @shared) are escape hatches, not daily syntax.
